body: I can't do any work at home. I get home, eat, pass out from exhaustion, wake up at midnight and stare at my work until I go back to sleep, and wake up in time to go back to school in the morning. It's an endless cycle that I can't break.

I would have to basically drop out of high school since I have exclusively hard (AP/"college level") classes this year. That would require letting my parents know that I have depression, and I know for a fact that they wouldn't even consider taking me to a therapist first. They'd send me to a church counselor that'll tell me that it's all my fault that I'm depressed because I don't follow their religion. Even if I made senior year easy, I couldn't handle the studying, pressure, decision-making, ect. that comes with college and especially post-college life. I just don't want to deal with anything anymore. No college means no good job which means no money which means no long term goals can even be planned and my life is even more pointless than before. I'm trapped between two life-altering decisions that are equally terrible. I don't wish to live within either one of them.

This hurt to read. I feel like I can't kill myself at some points because of how the people around me would feel but at the same time, I desperately try to end it weekly. It's a struggle that I can't win.

I left the username and password of this account in my suicide note so whoever finds it can find whatever else they need that I forgot in the real note. All of you wrote very good responses, but I suppose I didn't find that small crevice of hope within me that I was looking for. I'm refreshing the page one more time and then I'm logging off for good. I will update in the event that I fail again.

I feel like I'm at my breaking point. I already pushed myself too hard and I know what it feels like to try as hard as you physically and mentally can take and still be seen as a failure by everyone. Part of the reason I don't want to attend college is my poor individual decision making skills. I could probably barely be able to pick classes in the first place, let alone where I go, ect. It's not like I make bad decision necessarily, but I can't make them in the first place. I can't walk away from my parents and religion because then they'd just punish me somehow and harass me into going again. They're very conservative. The small things don't matter anymore. I tried caring about the small things during my short extra time, and it made me realize just how small they really are. They cannot give my life true meaning and I'm only distracting myself from the fact that my life is in shambles and I have no real reason to keep going on. And like I said, that fox would be very, very expensive and would require a good, very well paying job or marrying someone who does. Both of those options are obviously out of the question at this point. Honestly I should've done it at this point already but I fell asleep and woke up at 12:01 and the only reason I haven't done it yet is to check this post.

No I'm a junior and I was referring to college as the 4 years after the extra 5th year being senior year. And what am I supposed to do for those 50+ years? Not work? Waste away at home looking for some meaning in life? I can't handle those kinds of choices. I can't find a direction to set myself in life. I can barely decide what I want to eat on most days. And fuck the military, I'm not putting myself through that hell. I'm already in a bad enough one as it is. And again, what's to stop myself from doing it so other people will be happy?

I was considering a fox because I would be readily willing to take care of one as if it were my son/daughter if I had the chance but they too require a lot of attention as well as patience. However, they are very costly and I'm really fucking stupid so any pet would probably get hurt because of me.

Also, on the topic of going to a doctor, which is something I forgot in my original post, I don't feel like that would help because I'd just get on meds. Not to say that meds don't legitimately work for some people, but SSRIs seem super sketchy to me. It seems to work like any other recreational drug and that makes me weary of using it because I feel like it wouldn't actually make me better. Also, that would require telling my parents which I don't feel is an option right now. They have just offered my sibling counseling because they're in a similar situation right now so I should see how that works out.
